title: LLM Application Penetration Test (OWASP LLM Top 10)
summary: A scoped pentest of your LLM feature and the app around it: prompt injection, data disclosure, output handling, excessive agency and system-prompt leakage, with reproducible evidence.

seo.title: LLM Penetration Testing, OWASP LLM Top 10 | VipraTech
seo.description: Manual and automated pentest of LLM features against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, with reproducible transcripts, severity ratings and a retest.

problem.intro: Your product now has a chat assistant, a copilot or an AI search box, built on a hosted model with a system prompt, retrieval and perhaps a few tools. Your annual pentest covered the web app, but nobody has checked whether the model can be made to reveal its instructions, read another customer's data or pass unsafe output to the rest of your stack.

pain_points.title: Prompt injection, direct and indirect
pain_points.detail: Users can type instructions that override the system prompt, and documents, web pages or emails the model reads can carry instructions of their own.

pain_points.title: Sensitive data in the wrong answer
pain_points.detail: Retrieval, conversation history and tool results can expose another user's or tenant's data when access checks sit in the wrong layer.

pain_points.title: Model output trusted downstream
pain_points.detail: Output rendered as HTML or Markdown, passed to a database or another API, or used to trigger actions recreates classic injection risks in a new form.

pain_points.title: System prompts treated as secrets
pain_points.detail: System prompts often hold business rules, internal URLs or keys, and anything in a prompt should be assumed recoverable.

solution.overview: We run a scoped penetration test of your LLM feature and the application around it. Testing combines manual work by an experienced tester with automated probe sets run against your endpoint, so coverage is broad and the important findings are verified by hand. We test each OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications category that applies, from prompt injection and sensitive information disclosure to improper output handling, excessive agency, system prompt leakage, vector and embedding weaknesses and unbounded consumption. We also test the surrounding authentication, authorisation and API layer. Every finding includes a reproducible transcript or request, a severity rating, a MITRE ATLAS mapping where relevant and a specific fix. A retest confirms remediation.
capabilities: Threat model of the LLM feature: data flows, trust boundaries, tools and retrieval sources
Direct and indirect prompt injection testing, including content placed in retrieved documents
Data disclosure tests across users, roles and tenants
Output handling tests where model output reaches browsers, databases or other services
System prompt leakage and secrets exposure checks
Findings mapped to OWASP LLM Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS, with a retest

workflow.title: Agree scope and rules
workflow.detail: We agree the feature, environments, test accounts, rate limits and stop conditions in writing.

workflow.title: Threat model
workflow.detail: We map data flows, trust boundaries, retrieval sources, tools and every place model output goes.

workflow.title: Automated probing
workflow.detail: Probe sets for each relevant OWASP LLM category run against your endpoint, and every exchange is logged.

workflow.title: Manual testing
workflow.detail: A tester works through the feature by hand, chaining weaknesses and testing business context that automation misses.

workflow.title: Verify and rate
workflow.detail: Each candidate issue is reproduced, false positives are removed, and severity is agreed against real impact.

workflow.title: Report and retest
workflow.detail: You receive findings with evidence and fixes, and we retest after remediation.

human_in_the_loop: An experienced tester verifies every finding by hand before it reaches the report and agrees severity with your team. Automated probes widen coverage but never decide severity on their own.

faqs.q: Do you test the model provider itself?
faqs.a: No. We test your application: how you use the model, your prompts, retrieval, tools and output handling. Provider-side behaviour is noted where it affects you, but the scope is your product.
Automated probes are good for breadth and regression, but the most serious LLM findings usually come from chaining small weaknesses in your specific business context. That needs a human tester.

faqs.q: Can findings be shared with our customers?
faqs.a: Yes. We provide a full technical report for your team and a shorter summary you can share with customers under NDA.
A typical single-feature test takes two to three weeks including reporting. Larger scopes with agents, many tools or several tenants take longer, and we agree that before starting.
